newsitem.title: UK: UK Feb PMI index 53.5, further expanion in manuf.
newsitem.headline: UK Feb PMI index 53.5, further expanion in manuf.

text.p: British purchasing managers reported a further expansion in manufacturing activity in February for the ninth consecutive month, the Chartered Institute of Purchasing and Supply (CIPS) said.
But the purchasing managers' index (PMI) dipped slightly to a seasonally adjusted 53.5 from 53.9 in January, pointing to a very slight easing in the rate of growth.
"The continued expansion of the manufacturing economy largely reflected a strong rise in output during the month," the CIPS said.
"Output recorded the fastest growth since November 1994 as firms cleared backlogs of orders and rebuilt stocks of finished goods which had again been depleted through sales exceeding output."
The rate of growth of new orders remained strong but slowed slightly, leading to the modest weakening of the PMI.
"Orders from UK customers were reported to have remained buoyant but export orders grew only modestly," the CIPS said.
"The increasing strength of the pound, by making UK goods more expensive in overseas markets, was increasingly being blamed for lost orders."

However, the strong pound did benefit producers in the form of reduced prices for imported inputs. Overall input prices fell for the 16th consecutive month in February, which showed the sharpest monthly fall since last July.
Suppliers' delivery times lengthened only modestly, pointing to relatively subdued inflationary pressures.

The PMI was also weakened slightly by a moderate decline in the rate of growth of employment. Following is a table of seasonally adjusted PMI indices (Previously reported January figures in brackets):
FEBRUARY JANUARY
Purchasing Managers' Index 53.5 53.9 (54.0)
Quantity of purchases 54.3 53.3 (52.7)
Suppliers' Delivery Times 48.3 48.1 (48.2)
Stocks of Purchases 45.5 45.4 (45.6)
Stocks of Finished Goods 46.8 46.1 (46.1)
Employment 51.2 52.9 (53.1)

NOTE: The PMI is based on a weighted average of seasonally adjusted measures of output, new orders, suppliers' delivery times, stocks of items purchased and employment. A reading above 50 indicates that manufacturing is generally expanding, below 50 that it is generally declining.
-- Richard Murphy, London Newsroom 44 171 542 2774
